routes.reason: DY.0 (iteration, periodicity and dynamical moduli), DY.4 (equidistribution and small points, with dynamical applications) and DY.6 (families and canonical heights in families) are the natural homes for M_d and its critically marked cover, for the critical height with Ingram's comparison, and for equidistribution of PCF parameters. None of them yet constructs these objects, so the paper is a good source.

Nothing in the atlas plans Chow varieties of cycles. R09.1–R09.2 (projective parameter spaces, Hilbert and Quot schemes, boundedness) is the closest owner, and Chow varieties of bounded-degree cycles are built from the same machinery (Kollár, Rational Curves, Ch. I).

PAPER-YUAN-26 proposes this Part II with a brief covering Yuan–Zhang adelic divisors on quasi-projective schemes, Deligne pairings, non-degeneracy and the height inequality. DMY consumes the same theory (invariant extensions, the relative-dimension-0 Deligne pairing, [YZ, Thm. 1.3.2], Thms. 5.3.3 and 5.4.3), so coalescing there is right. The projective equidistribution theorem stays with DY.4, which is how PAPER-YUAN-26 records it.

Heights of cycles and Gao–Ge–Kühne Lemma 4.3 are already in the uniformity Part II (PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26 routes Lemma 4.3 there as its item 58), so this route only adds a consumer and duplicates nothing.

No atlas layer treats complex dynamics in parameter space. The only hits for bifurcation, currents or plurisubharmonic functions are unrelated: Tau Ceti GeometricTopology's Thurston geometries, and the real Monge–Ampère theory in OptimalTransport. A Part II of ArithmeticDynamics, like ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIMarkoff, is right. The brief is amended in three ways. It imports subharmonic potential theory from Tau Ceti PDE, Lane C. It carries the corrections E7–E9. Its acceptance test no longer asks for the DeMarco–Wang–Ye theorem, which the paper uses only as an input.
